words: واتقوا فتنة لا تصيبن الذين ظلموا منكم خاصة
rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet reports that when God wills a people to be punished, the punishment reaches those among them, who are then resurrected according to their deeds.
rows.anchor: وقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا اراد الله بقوم عذابا أصاب من كان منهم ثم يبعثون

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says an initiator of a good practice earns its reward and an initiator of a bad one bears its sin and the followers' burden; the source also links this to Adam's sons.
rows.anchor: وقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم من سن فى الإسلام سنة حسنة فله أجرها وأجر من عمل بها

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Asked which charity is greatest, the Prophet answers: giving while healthy and reluctant, before one delays until death approaches.
rows.anchor: وقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم فى جواب من سأله أي الصدقة أعظم قال أن تصدق وأنت صحيح شحيح

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says the upper hand is better than the lower; the lower hand is the receiver and the upper the giver, with the loan verse offered as support.
rows.anchor: وقوله اليد العليا خير من اليد السفلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The giver's charity depends on a recipient accepting the due owed to God, which purifies the giver; without a receiving hand, the wealthy could not give charity.
rows.anchor: أن العطية من أيدينا مفتقرة إلى من يضع فيها حقا وجب عليها

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says that when God intends good for someone, He grants that person understanding of religion.
rows.anchor: وقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم من يرد الله به خيرا يفقهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author links the verses about creatures' glorification and human failure to comprehend it with God's wide forgiveness for those on earth who do not glorify or understand that praise.
rows.anchor: ثم أعلم سبحانه سعة مغفرته لمن فى الأرض الذين لا يسبحونه ولا يفقهون تسبيح المسبحين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says that failure to understand God is the punitive seal placed on people for turning away.
rows.anchor: ثم أعلم بالعلة التى لأجلها حرموا الفقه عن ربهم وأن ذلك هو ختم عقوبة الإعراض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition ʿan can mark substitution, as in a soul's inability to avail another soul.
rows.anchor: وتجئ للبدل نحو ﴿ واتقوا يوما لا تجزي نفس عن نفس شيئا ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author gives ʿan the sense of ʿalā, over or against, in the statement that the miser harms himself.
rows.anchor: وللاستعلاء نحو ﴿ ومن يبخل فإنما يبخل عن نفسه ﴾

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: One explanation takes ʿan as indicating preference: Solomon put the love of good ahead of remembrance of his Lord.
rows.anchor: إني أحببت حب الخير عن ذكر ربي

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: Another explanation keeps ʿan in its basic sense: Solomon was turning away from remembrance of his Lord.
rows.anchor: وقيل على بابها اي منصرفا عن ذكر ربي

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu ʿUbayda related aḥbabtu to a camel kneeling; by semantic inclusion, ʿan attaches to that sense, and love of good is causal.
rows.anchor: وحكى الرماني عن أبي عبيدة إن احببت من احب البعير احبابا اذا برك فلم يقم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAn can mark cause: Abraham's prayer followed a promise, and Lot's people say they will not abandon their gods because of Muhammad's statement.
rows.anchor: وما نحن بتاركي آلهتنا عن قولك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author also gives ʿan the sense of after, citing soon afterward, words displaced from their places, and passage from one stage to another.
rows.anchor: عما قليل ليصبحن نادمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAn may mean min, from; the author supports this with verses accepting repentance and deeds from people, comparing the latter wording with the story of Adam's sons.
rows.anchor: أولئك الذين نتقبل عنهم أحسن ما عملوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author lists a reading of ʿan as equivalent to bi in the statement that the Prophet does not speak from desire.
rows.anchor: وما ينطق عن الهوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects the literal, distancing interpretation because it would imply that the Prophet speaks while actually subject to desire.
rows.anchor: فيلزم إن يكون النطق حال كونه متلبسا بالهوى وهو فاسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAsā expresses hope for something desired and apprehension about something disliked; both uses occur together in this verse.
rows.anchor: وعسى أن تكرهوا شيئا وهو خير لكم

rows.speaker: ابن فارس
rows.claim: Ibn Fāris says ʿasā can mean that something is near or approaching.
rows.anchor: قال ابن فارس وتاتي للقرب والدنوا

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisāʾī says every Qur'anic ʿasā used as a declarative report is singular.
rows.anchor: وقال الكسائي كل ما في القرآن من عسى على وجه الخبر فهو موحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A dual expression can intend one of its two referents: pearls emerge from the salt sea alone, although the verse says from both; the author also cites fish and jewelry from the two seas.
rows.anchor: كقوله تعالى ﴿ يخرج منهما اللؤلؤ والمرجان ﴾ 1 وإنما يخرج من أحدهما

rows.speaker: أبو ذؤيب الهذلي
rows.claim: The author says Abu Dhuʾayb wrongly describes the Furat flowing over a pearl, since only the salty water does so.
rows.anchor: وقد غلط في هذا المعنى أبو ذؤيب الهذلي حيث قال يذكر الدرة

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī says the wording cannot mean a man from both Mecca and al-Ṭāʾif; it means a man from either city.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو علي في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural expression that God placed the moon among them means in one of the heavens.
rows.anchor: وجعل القمر فيهن نورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the verse attributes forgetting to both Moses and his companion, Joshua alone forgot the fish; the attribution includes Moses because he remained silent.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى ﴿ نسيا حوتهما ﴾ 1 والناسى كان يوشع بدليل قوله

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: One explanation says the days refer to the second day of the pilgrimage and that the person who stays longer is treated like the one who hastens.
rows.anchor: والتعجيل يكون في اليوم الثاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author offers another possible sense: neither pilgrim should accuse the other of falling short.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يراد لا يقولن أحدهما لصاحبه أنت مقصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dual reference to both parents is distributed individually: each parent receives one sixth.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى ﴿ ولأبويه لكل واحد منهما السدس ﴾

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: One reported interpretation takes the dual verb as referring to just one of the two parents.
rows.anchor: أي أحدهما على أحد القولين

words: فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِمَا فِيمَا ٱفْتَدَتْ بِهِۦ
rows.speaker: أبو بكر الصيرفي
rows.claim: Al-Ṣayrafī says the husband bears the wrong by taking compensation; the verse permits a ransom when failure to uphold God's limits is feared, without requiring both spouses to fail.
rows.anchor: قال أبو بكر الصيرفي المعنى فإن خيف من ذلك جازت الفدية وليس الشرط أن يجتمعا

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: One view takes the dual imperative as addressed to one angel.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى ﴿ ألقيا في جهنم ﴾ 6 قيل هو خطاب للملك

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad says the dual form repeats the singular command, meaning cast, cast; he applies the same analysis to qifā.
rows.anchor: وقال المبرد ثناه على ألق والمعنى ألق ألق

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abū Isḥāq disagrees: the command addresses two angels.
rows.anchor: وخالفه أبو إسحاق وقال بل هو مخاطبة للملكين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author supplies an omitted referent for that: they should rejoice in that statement.
rows.anchor: وأما قوله تعالى ﴿ فبذلك فليفرحوا ﴾ 6 أي بذلك القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In reciprocal ellipsis, speech contains paired counterparts but omits one member where the parallel member makes it clear.
rows.anchor: السابع الحذف المقابلي وهو أن يجتمع في الكلام متقابلان فيحدف من واحد منهما مقابلة لدلالة الاخر عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse omits reciprocal clauses: if I fabricated, my crime is mine and you are free of it; your crime is yours and I am free of it.
rows.anchor: الأصل فإن افتريته فعلى إجرامي وأنتم براء منه وعليكم إجرامكم وأنا برىء مما تجرمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge to bring a sign like those sent to earlier peoples omits the conditional idea that those earlier messengers were sent with signs.
rows.anchor: ومنه قوله تعالى ﴿ فليأتنا بآية كما أرسل الأولون ﴾ 2 تقديره أن أرسل فليأتنا بآية

words: وَيُعَذِّبَ ٱلْمُنَٰفِقِينَ إِن شَآءَ أَوْ يَتُوبَ عَلَيْهِمْ
rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Commentators restore the omitted counterparts: God may punish without granting repentance, or grant repentance and then not punish; this is bounded by worldly life.
rows.anchor: تقديره كما قال المفسرون ويعذب المنافقين إن شاء فلا يتوب عليهم أو يتوب عليهم فلا يعذبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ellipsis means intercourse is forbidden until menstruation stops and the woman bathes; the author says context decisively supports this Shāfiʿī ruling.
rows.anchor: وأعلم أن دلالة السياق قاطعة بهذه المحذوفات وبهذا التقدير يعتضد القول بالمنع من وطء الحائض إلا بعد الطهر والتطهر جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to put the hand in the shirt omits that it goes in, and the result clause omits the command to take it out.
rows.anchor: تقديره أدخل يدك تدخل وأخرجها تخرج إلا أنه قد عرض في هذه المادة تناسب بالطباق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the cited verse, antithesis keeps the usual pairing of the first with the third element and the second with the fourth.
rows.anchor: نسبة الأول إلى الثالث ونسبة الثاني إلى الرابع على حالة الأكثرية

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The author cites a line comparing a remembered person's shiver to a bird shaking off raindrops as evidence for the paired construction.
rows.anchor: كما انتفض العصفور بللة القطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the trade and amusement verse, the pronoun returns to the more distant trade: it distracts more people from worship, is more useful, or was primary while amusement accompanied its arrival.
rows.anchor: أعاده في الآية الأولى على التجارة وإن كانت أبعد ومؤنثة لأنها أجذب لقلوب العباد عن طاعة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the verse about accusing an innocent person, the pronoun returns to sin because sin is the nearer and more salient antecedent.
rows.anchor: واعاده في الآية الثانية على الإثم رعاية لمرتبة القرب والتذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A plural pronoun can refer to two people because duals count as plural in meaning; here it means Solomon and David.
rows.anchor: يعني حكم سليمان وداود وقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural demonstrative أولئك refers to the two people Aisha and Ṣafwān.
rows.anchor: فأوقع أولئك وهو جمع على عائشة وصفوان

rows.speaker: قالوا
rows.claim: A dual pronoun may refer to one of the two antecedents; they say the pearl comes from only one sea.
rows.anchor: قالوا وإنما يخرج من أحدهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A dual pronoun can also refer to a pair even though only the young companion forgot the fish.
rows.anchor: وقوله ﴿ نسيا حوتهما ﴾ 7 وإنما نسيه الفتى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in then We made him a drop attaches to the human but refers to his offspring, since Adam was not created from a drop.
rows.anchor: فهذا لولده لأن آدم لم يخلق من نطفة

rows.speaker: ابن حذافة
rows.claim: One occasion report says Ibn Ḥudhāfa asked the Prophet who his father was, was told Ḥudhāfa, and was distressed by the answer.
rows.anchor: قيل نزلت في ابن حذافة حين قال للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من أبي

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: Another occasion report places the verse in the Hajj context, when people asked whether pilgrimage was required every year.
rows.anchor: وقيل نزلت في الحج حين قالوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The later pronoun points to other religious matters whose knowledge is needed, not to the previously mentioned questions; the author argues that سألها treats them as a direct object.
rows.anchor: يريد إن تسألوا عن اشياء أخر من دينكم بكم إلى علمها حاجة تبد لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because leaning toward wrongdoers means inclination or reliance, the verse describes its lesser penalty as touching fire, below the punishment for oppression itself.
rows.anchor: لما نهى عن الركون إلى الظالمين وهو الميل إليهم والاعتماد عليهم وكان دون ذلك مشاركتهم في الظلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Normally, where a verb has a direct object and an oblique object, the direct object precedes the prepositional phrase; the source compares this with the ordering in 48:24.
rows.anchor: فإن كان في الكلام مفعولان أحدهما يعدى وصول الفعل إليه بالحرف والآخر بنفسه قدم ما تعدى إليه الفعل بنفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first clause reverses the ordinary order to avoid a heavy run of nearby articulation points in بسطت ... لتقتلني.
rows.anchor: مانع أقوى وهو مخافة أن يتوالى ثلاثة أحرف متقاربات المخرج فيثقل الكلام بسبب ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second clause uses an active participle instead of a finite verb to make the comparison apt; with the sound obstacle gone, it follows the usual object order.
rows.anchor: لما أمن هذا المحذور في عجز الآية لما اقتضته البلاغة من الإتيان باسم الفاعل موضع الجملة الفعلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word order reflects the contrast: the first brother is eager to aggress and is expressed with a verb, while the other denies aggression and is expressed with a participle.
rows.anchor: لما كان الأول حريصا على التعدي على الغير قدم المتعدى على الآلة فقال إلى يدك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author classifies coordination with God, the Messenger, and believers as a mode of magnification, alongside other pairings of God with the Messenger, angels, or people of knowledge.
rows.anchor: إن الله وملائكته يصلون على النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition bi can mean ʿalā, over: entrusting someone with a qinṭār is expressed as trusting him over it.
rows.anchor: ومن أهل الكتاب من إن تأمنه بقنطار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author explains the phrase about mocking passersby as meaning that they gesture at them, using the parallel wording عليهم as support.
rows.anchor: وإذا مروا بهم يتغامزون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bal can cancel the preceding claim and assert the correction: God has not taken a child; they are honored servants.
rows.anchor: فالأول الإضراب فيه إما بمعنى ترك الأول والرجوع عنه بإبطاله وتسمى حرف ابتداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same corrective use of bal retracts the charge that the Messenger is possessed and asserts that he brought the truth.
rows.anchor: أم يقولون به جنة بل جاءهم بالحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here bal shifts from the scene of people arriving singly to another, more important topic: their former claim that no appointment was made for them.
rows.anchor: بل زعمتم ألن نجعل لكم موعدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the passage about the charge that the Messenger fabricated the revelation, bal moves from the first story to a more important one.
rows.anchor: انتقل من القصة الأولى إلى ما هو أهم منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the succession of statements about the afterlife, bal is not a topic shift; it asserts that the people possess the listed states of ignorance, doubt, and blindness.
rows.anchor: ليست للانتقال بل هم متصفون بهذه الصفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bal does not retract their same-sex acts or neglect of women; it clarifies their transgression and shifts to naming their further faults.
rows.anchor: والمراد تعديد خطاياهم واتصافهم بهذه الصفات وبل لم ينو ما أضافه إليهم من إتيان الذكور والإعراض عن الإناث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects al-Basīṭ's and Ibn Mālik's claim that Qur'anic bal only marks transition, since the Qur'an also uses it to retract and correct.
rows.anchor: وزعم صاحب البسيط وابن مالك أنها لا تقع في القرآن إلا بهذا المعنى وليست كذلك

rows.speaker: ابن الحاجب
rows.claim: Ibn al-Ḥājib says bal after an affirmative clause would be a correction or slip, absent from Qur'an and eloquent speech; after negation it may correct or affirm the second clause.
rows.anchor: وكذا قال ابن الحاجب في شرح المفصل إبطال ما للأول وإثباته للثاني إن كان في الإثبات

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Commentators read mā as interrogative: by what did my Lord forgive me?
rows.anchor: فقال المفسرون معناه بأي شىء غفر لي

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisāʾī reads mā as a verbal noun: by my Lord's forgiveness.
rows.anchor: وقال الكسائي معناه بمغفرة ربي فجعلها مصدرية

rows.speaker: الهروي
rows.claim: Al-Harawī notes that retaining the alif in interrogative mā joined to a preposition is a dialect.
rows.anchor: قال الهروي إثبات الألف في ما بمعنى الاستفهام مع اتصالها بحرف الجر لغة

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: One reading makes mā interrogative, asking how Satan was led astray, then starts a new oath clause.
rows.anchor: فقيل إنها للاستفهام أي بأي شىء أغويتني ثم ابتدأ

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: A second reading makes mā a verbal noun and attaches bi to an omitted oath verb: because You led me astray, I swear I will waylay them.
rows.anchor: وقيل مصدرية والباء متعلقة بفعل القسم المحذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another analysis takes bi itself as an oath, since Satan was morally accountable and divine responsibility is worthy of an oath.
rows.anchor: ويجوز إن تكون الباء للقسم أي فأقسم بإغوائك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath lām prevents attaching bi directly to لأقعدن; the author illustrates that one cannot say والله لا بزيد لأمرن.
rows.anchor: قيل يصد عنه لام القسم إلا ترى انك لا تقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author classifies mā in the two Qur'anic exclamations as exclamatory; there is no third example except in Saʿīd ibn Jubayr's reading of 82:6.
rows.anchor: والرابع التعجبية كقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr reads mā in the question about what deceived the human as exclamatory.
rows.anchor: إلا في قراءة سعيد بن جبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In exclamatory constructions mā is nominative as the subject, while the following clause is its predicate; exclamation and interrogation are closely related.
rows.anchor: وتكون في موضع رفع بالابتداء وما خبر وهو قريب مما قبله لأن الاستفهام والتعجب بينهما تلازم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā may be an indefinite noun modified by an adjective or clause, as in 'a mosquito or something beyond it' and 'how excellent a thing He exhorts you with'.
rows.anchor: والخامس نكرة بمعنى شىء ويلزمها النعت كقولك رأيت ما معجبا لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In فنعما هي, mā is an indefinite noun without a modifier or relative clause, accusative as specification, meaning 'a good thing'.
rows.anchor: أي فنعم شيئا هي كما تقول نعم رجلا زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā can be elided in expressions such as 'when you see there', 'this is a separation between me and you', and 'what was between you was severed'.
rows.anchor: فائدة قال بعضهم وقد تجىء ما مضمرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thumma can mark temporal delay or a non-temporal progression in qualities, highlighting the importance of what follows and prompting reflection rather than ordering events in time.
rows.anchor: والحاصل انها للتراخي في الزمان وهو المعبر عنه بالمهلة وتكون للتباين في الصفات وغيرها من غير قصد مهلة زمانية

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: Some grammarians say thumma can signal astonishment, as in the unbelievers equating their Lord and the arrogant person's hope for more.
rows.anchor: ثم الذين كفروا بربهم يعدلون

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: Some take thumma as equivalent to wāw in these examples, but the author says it retains its original sense.
rows.anchor: فإلينا مرجعهم ثم الله شهيد

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: Because the angels were ordered to bow before humans were created, one explanation treats the sequence as saying that God formed humanity and then commanded the angels.
rows.anchor: وقد أمر الله الملائكة بالسجود قبل خلقنا فالمعنى وصورناكم

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: Another explanation keeps temporal order: God began humanity's creation with Adam from clay and later formed him, and began each person's creation from a drop before forming him.
rows.anchor: وقيل على بابها والمعنى ابتدأنا خلقكم لان الله تعالى خلق آدم من تراب ثم صوره وابتدأ خلق الانسان من نطفة ثم صوره

words: خَلَقَكُم مِّن طِينٍ ثُمَّ قَضَىٰٓ أَجَلًۭا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the term was already decreed, the sequence reports the order in which God tells the audience: first about creation from clay, then about the term.
rows.anchor: وقد كان قضى الاجل فمعناه اخبركم اني خلقته من طين ثم اخبركم اني قضيت الاجل

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: Some call thumma redundant in the account of the three who stayed behind because their repentance is already the answer to the preceding ḥattā idhā clause.
rows.anchor: لان تاب جواب اذا من قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the conditional about fighting, the raised verb after thumma starts a new report instead of continuing the conditional consequence.
rows.anchor: فان قيل ما المانع من الجزم على العطف فالجواب انه عدل به عن حكم الجزاء إلى حكم الاخبار ابتداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the verb were jussive, lack of help would be limited to fighting; the indicative makes their defeat an unrestricted promise and lasting condition.
rows.anchor: لو جزم لكان نفي النصر مقيدا بمقاتلتهم كتوليهم وحين رفع كان النصر وعدا مطلقا

rows.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر
rows.claim: Al-Qāḍī Abū Bakr says the Prophet never explicitly identified each passage as Meccan or Medinan; Companions and Successors learned chronology through their preservation and attention to revelation.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي أبو بكر فى الانتصار إنما هذا يرجع لحفظ الصحابة وتابعيهم

rows.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر
rows.claim: Since full Meccan–Medinan classification was not an obligatory duty, reports were not exhaustively transmitted; scholars may disagree or use reason, except where chronology is needed to identify abrogation.
rows.anchor: وإنما لم يفعله أنه لم يؤمر به ولم يجعل الله علم ذلك من فرائض الأمة

rows.speaker: قوم من الفقهاء والمتكلمين
rows.claim: Some jurists and theologians would establish Qur'anic material through a solitary report without widespread transmission; the people of truth reject this.
rows.anchor: ذهب قوم من الفقهاء والمتكلمين إلى إثبات قرآن حكما لا علما بخبر الواحد دون الاستفاضة وكره ذلك أهل الحق

rows.speaker: قوم من المتكلمين
rows.claim: Some theologians allow reasoned selection of linguistically correct readings even without proof that the Prophet recited them; the author says the people of truth reject and condemn this.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم من المتكلمين إنه يسوغ إعمال الرأي والاجتهاد فى إثبات قراءة وأوجه وأحرف إذا كانت تلك الأوجه صوابا فى اللغة العربية

rows.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر
rows.claim: Al-Qāḍī Abū Bakr says transmission is established by a sufficient community to yield tawātur, not by unanimous agreement; a later dispute does not erase an already widespread transmission.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي وقد رد الله عنه طعن الطاعنين واختلاف الضالين وليس المعتبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author invokes God's promise to preserve the Reminder and collect and recite the Qur'an against claims of additions, omissions, or textual alteration.
rows.anchor: وبذلك يسقط اعتراض الملحدين فى القرآن وذلك دليل على صحة نقل القرآن وحفظه وصيانته من التغيير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The community agrees that preservation means guarding the Qur'an for practice and from error or confusion, which warrants certainty in the communal codex.
rows.anchor: وأجمعت الأمة أن المراد بذلك حفظه على المكلفين للعمل به وحراسته من وجوه الغلط والتخليط

rows.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر
rows.claim: Al-Qāḍī Abū Bakr says the two protective sūras are Qur'an and their transmission is as widespread as that of the whole Qur'an; reports that Ibn Masʿūd denied them are unsound.
rows.anchor: والمعوذتان من القرآن واستفاضتهما كاستفاضة جميع القرآن وأما ما روي عن ابن مسعود قال القاضي أبو بكر فلم يصح عنه

rows.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر
rows.claim: Al-Qāḍī says it is impermissible to attribute rejection or alteration of a Qur'anic verse or letter to a Companion on solitary reports.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز أن يضاف إلى عبد الله أو إلى أبي بن كعب أو زيد أو عثمان أو علي أو واحد من ولده

rows.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر
rows.claim: Al-Qāḍī says the qunūt words in Ubayy ibn Kaʿb's codex are supplication, not Qur'an; the idea that they were revealed then abrogated is possible but unproven.
rows.anchor: وأن كلام القنوت المروى عن أبي بن كعب أثبته في مصحفه لم تقم حجة بأنه قرآن منزل
